units.function: Unit tests for resolving local plugin build watch targets and restarting a loaded plugin worker after debounced development-file changes.
units.dependencyDirection: Local package metadata/files are interpreted by plugin-dev-watcher; plugin lifecycle loaded events resolve a package path; chokidar observes concrete targets; a debounced callback invokes lifecycle.restartWorker for the plugin ID.
units.keyDataModels: Plugin package root/package.json paperclipPlugin entrypoints; manifest/worker/UI/dist files; watch target path/recursive/kind; plugin.loaded identity; filesystem all event; restartWorker and watcher lifecycle.
units.lifecycle: Resolve declared runtime files or enumerate dist fallback; begin watching when a local plugin loads; coalesce a file change; restart its worker; close watchers and timers.
units.testAssessment: All four tests pass. Watching concrete output files and debouncing restart are sensible development patterns, and the loaded-plugin resolver avoids eagerly watching unknown packages. Missing tests leave the critical boundary unproved: strict development-only enablement, canonical path containment for manifest ../ or symlinks, file add/delete, plugin unload/reinstall, multiple-plugin event isolation, repeated burst semantics, restart serialization/failure/backoff, close during pending timer and large-tree resource limits.
units.designRationale: Shorten local plugin development feedback by automatically restarting only the affected worker when compiled entrypoints or metadata change.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe extension development without allowing file watchers or unsigned hot reload to enter managed-cloud/self-hosted production trust boundaries.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT only for an explicit local development Profile. Require a startup-level non-overridable production prohibition; canonicalize every target with realpath and prove it remains under an approved plugin root; reject symlink/path escape and unbounded fallback scans; serialize restarts per plugin; cancel timers/watchers on unload; handle add/delete and failed restart with bounded backoff; display a persistent unsafe-development state. Production upgrades must use signed immutable packages, staged health checks and rollback rather than watchers.
units.responsibilityConflict: Hot reload changes executable plugin behavior without a release approval, provenance record or responsibility decision. That is acceptable only in a declared developer environment and must never become a path for production Connector or approval logic mutation.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: declared concrete runtime targets reduce watch breadth; changes are debounced; restart is keyed to one plugin; close is exposed. CRITICAL deployment gate gap: no test proves the watcher is impossible to enable in production. HIGH path gap: manifest entrypoint traversal and symlink escape are untested. HIGH supply-chain gap: changed code is executed without signature/hash or approval by design. MEDIUM lifecycle gap: unload/reinstall, pending timer cancellation, concurrent restart and failure/backoff are absent. MEDIUM resource gap: fallback dist enumeration has no tested file/depth cap. LOW disclosure: logs include full local package paths, which is useful in development but should remain outside customer telemetry by default.
